note: On profile he is close to ideal: founder of a creative agency, formerly a lawyer, a copywriter at McCann, a ministerial spokesperson, a columnist and six and a half years at Google. He is explicitly good-to-great — training twenty-one years, visible abs used as his own dietary barometer, fine-tuning a modality switch rather than rescuing anything — and about as far from the deconditioned gym-averse exclusion as the corpus contains. He fails on the two criteria that decide deals. Income: $6,000 'would have been the highest training plan I've ever paid in my life', and as a one-year-old agency founder his constraint is allocation, not affluence. And health is emphatically not his neglected area — blood work every four to six months, five eggs a morning, daily stretching, three sessions a week for two decades. This is almost exactly the Badrane Hriouch profile already assessed in the ICP file: fits on profile, fails on willingness to pay. The instructive difference is what the rep did with it. In that case the rep recognised it live and disqualified rather than discounted; here the rep pre-emptively told the prospect the price would not suit his budget, quoted it anyway, and then routed him to a $200/month product. Both are defensible outcomes for the deal and they produce very different revenue, which is a reason the stated ICP needs a rule attached to it rather than just a description.
